QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_71

question.text: Svasti Microfinance (Section 8 FPE) claims 72% of E-Diksha-style participants borrowed formal loans vs moneylenders (matching E-Diksha 72% formal-credit indicator). The SIA's MOST critical audit step is:

answer.text: Verify via (i) partner-lender disbursement-register match, (ii) beneficiary loan-card / passbook photo, (iii) interest-rate comparison showing formal-credit rate materially lower than prior moneylender rate, (iv) credit-bureau (CIBIL-MFI bureau) enquiry trail

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Formal-credit-access claims need lender-side disbursement data, beneficiary primary document (loan card / passbook), interest-rate evidence (to show the shift is beneficial not just nominal), and credit-bureau trail (MFI CICs track microfinance borrowing). Four-source triangulation is SAS-1300's robust MoV. **The Trap:** Options A, C, D are single-source or irrelevant. **Cross-Exam Context:** Credit-bureau checks also in XXIV (AML — customer-risk profiling) and V-A (MF Distributor — loan referral). **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Always capture the interest-rate delta — a participant who shifted from 36% moneylender to 24% MFI achieved nominal inclusion but still pays high interest. The SIA should report BOTH the access and the pricing improvement.
